data.narrative:
Gilmour Space Technologies is a Series D-stage space and aerospace company that has raised approximately A$100M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 4 private companies at Series C–D stage (Sierra Space, Apex Space, Varda Space Industries, Skyryse) and 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier to the A$100M raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $150M. Peer-median analysis across the 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies produces a median valuation of $1.9B, with a range of $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because the target's revenue is not disclosed. This is typical for private-stage companies and limits the utility of the 25.3x median P/S multiple observed across the public Space & Aerospace universe.

The two applicable methods produce a wide triangulated range of $128M to $2.2B, with a median of $1.0B. The disparity reflects structural differences between stage-progression (conservative, capital-based) and peer-median approaches (market-based). Key uncertainties include customer traction, technology validation, and near-term capital deployment plans—factors that would narrow this range and anchor valuation toward the peer median or above.
